llm.summary: The skill mostly fits its RiteKit connector purpose, but its first-time setup tells users to run unverified remote installer scripts directly in a shell.

dimensions.detail: Routine operation is scoped to Bash(oo *) and is proportionate, but the documented setup fallback can execute mutable remote code under the invoking user's account, which is higher-impact than normal RiteKit data lookups.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The first-time setup includes curl-to-bash and Invoke-RestMethod-to-Invoke-Expression installer commands for the oo CLI without version pinning, checksum/signature verification, or explicit user approval before local software installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation language says to use the skill for any RiteKit request, which is broad, but the runtime instructions stay focused on RiteKit connector schema inspection and connector execution.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not show backdoors, scheduled tasks, privilege escalation, or hidden persistence, but installing a CLI can make durable local environment changes that are not described in detail.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose is coherent: it uses the OOMOL oo CLI to call RiteKit connector actions, with credentials handled server-side and no raw token handling in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the first-time setup carefully before installing. Prefer installing the oo CLI through a verified official release or package manager, and do not let an agent run the remote installer commands automatically without your explicit approval.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: Installing the oo CLI is related to the stated connector purpose, but the direct remote-script execution pattern is a material supply-chain concern because it lacks integrity checks and could run changed code later.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad RiteKit trigger language is overinclusive, but it remains bounded to RiteKit-related tasks and does not by itself show hidden or unrelated behavior.
[T03] expected: The static finding is supported by the artifact at the bash and PowerShell installer commands; this supports Review rather than malicious because the commands are disclosed setup instructions for the required CLI, not covert payload retrieval.
